To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the structure-first approach is better for queries with complex structural constraints and the keyword-first approach is better when the full-text predicates are complex.

the structure-first approach outperforms the keyword-first approach in terms of the query time, and the keyword-first approach outperformed the structure-first approach in terms the number of results returned.
The keyword-first approach is more efficient in terms of the number of elements retrieved.

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

, the structure-first approach is the better choice for processing the query which consists of a few keywords, while the keyword-first approach is the preferred approach for the queries with more keywords.
the keyword-first approach performs better in terms of query response time and the structure-first approach is superior in terms of the number of returned results.

the structure-first approach is the better choice for the queries with complex structural constraints and few keywords, while the keyword-first approach is the preferred approach when the query is full of keywords and the structural constraints are simple.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the structure-first approach is better for queries which have a small number of keywords and a small number of elements, while the keyword-first approach is more suitable for queries which have many keywords but a small number of required elements.

, for the XML data with a small average depth and a small keyword density, the structure-first approach would be more efficient; for the XML data whose keywords are distributed evenly in the document, the keyword-first would be more efficient.
, in general, the structure-first approach is more efficient than the keyword-first approach.
The main takeaway from our work is that
it is possible to achieve a high performance on the processing of XML queries with structural constraints and full-text constraints.
a query processor can be more efficient if the order of processing structural and full-text constraints is chosen appropriately.
it is possible to achieve high query performance by exploiting the structure and the keywords within an XML document.
